primary_claim: A base Llama-3-8B model produces no structured role- or goal-oriented language under empty or single-token prompts, but minimal instruction priming (e.g. 'You are a helpful assistant.') reliably induces structured role-based self-talk language, unlike the instruction-tuned version which shows such language immediately.

effect.metric: regex-detected role/goal-language hit rate across prompt conditions
effect.value: base model: 0 regex hits for role/goal patterns across 20 iterations under empty/single-token prompts; role-based language appeared consistently after minimal instruction priming

contradicts_or_qualifies: Prior BOS-token and recursive prompt tests mainly used instruction-tuned models rather than base models to test recursive null/minimal prompt behaviour
stated_future_work: Replicate across Mistral 7B Base and possibly Qwen
Clean up process, e.g. trim repetition when feeding output back
Long term: release a small evaluation script and potential benchmark for alignment researchers
limitations_stated: Initial runs were contaminated by CLI interface outputs the author failed to control
All metrics are based on simple regex matching, which is not yet robust
Small sample size (~20 iterations per condition); this is an exploratory pilot, not a rigorous benchmark
Special characters in syntactic formatting often made dialogue-condition output less intelligible than other conditions
quote: Across ~20 iterations per condition, the base model produced no structured output under empty or single-token prompts, with structured role-based language appearing consistently only after minimal instruction priming.
